terms.definition: Ibn ʿUthaymīn defines the aḥkām as what the address of the Lawgiver concerning the acts of the mukallafūn requires, by way of demand (ṭalab), choice (takhyīr) or positing (waḍʿ). Demand covers command and prohibition, binding or preferential; choice is the mubāḥ; positing is the waḍʿī ruling. Ibn al-Laḥḥām separates khiṭāb al-waḍʿ, which can attach to the acts of a child or madman, from khiṭāb al-taklīf, which does not bind them.
conditions: three modes: ṭalab, takhyīr, waḍʿ
taklīf requires ʿaql and understanding the address (Ibn al-Laḥḥām q2)

refs.note: Definition: what the Lawgiver's address requires by ṭalab, takhyīr or waḍʿ.

refs.excerpt_ar: والمراد بقولنا: «من طلب»؛ الأمر والنهي سواء على سبيل الإلزام، أو الأفضلية.
refs.note: Ibn ʿUthaymīn: ṭalab covers command and prohibition, binding (ilzām) or preferential (afḍaliyya).
Condition of taklīf is ʿaql and understanding the address; distinguishes khiṭāb al-waḍʿ from khiṭāb al-taklīf.

terms.definition: The part of the ḥukm consisting of demand (to do or to refrain, bindingly or not) or choice. In Ibn ʿUthaymīn it is the five statuses wājib, mandūb, muḥarram, makrūh and mubāḥ, each defined by whether there is a command or prohibition and whether it is binding.
conditions: applies to the mukallaf (bāligh and ʿāqil)

refs.note: The ṭalab/takhyīr part of the definition of al-aḥkām.

refs.excerpt_ar: والمراد بقولنا: «من طلب»؛ الأمر والنهي سواء على سبيل الإلزام، أو الأفضلية.
refs.note: Ṭalab = command and prohibition, binding or preferential; takhyīr = mubāḥ.
Taklīf does not bind the child or the madman (only khiṭāb al-waḍʿ attaches to their acts).

terms.definition: Ibn ʿUthaymīn: what the Lawgiver has posited as signs (amārāt) of the establishment or negation, the effectiveness or nullity, of something; among them validity and invalidity. The waḍʿī elements include sabab, sharṭ and māniʿ; Ibn Qudāma says that setting something as a condition or impediment of a ruling is itself a sharʿī ruling.
conditions: validity requires the conditions present and the impediments absent (Ibn ʿUthaymīn)

refs.excerpt_ar: الأحكام الوضعية: ما وضعه الشارع من أمارات، لثبوت أو انتفاء، أو نفوذ، أو إلغاء.
refs.note: Definition of al-aḥkām al-waḍʿiyya as signs posited by the Lawgiver; ṣiḥḥa and fasād are among them.

refs.excerpt_ar: وعكس الشرط: المانع: وهو: ما يلزم من وجوده عدم الحكم
refs.note: Ibn Qudāma: the māniʿ as the converse of the sharṭ (the following sentence calls positing them a sharʿī ruling).
Khiṭāb al-waḍʿ attaches to the acts of those not under taklīf.

terms.definition: What the Lawgiver commanded by way of binding (ʿalā wajh al-ilzām), e.g. the five prayers. Ibn al-Laḥḥām reports two narrations from Aḥmad on farḍ and wājib: in the soundest they are synonyms; in the other farḍ is stronger (e.g. established by a decisive proof).
conditions: a command (amr)
binding (ilzām)

refs.note: Farḍ and wājib synonymous in the soundest narration; the other narration makes farḍ stronger.

refs.excerpt_ar: الوجوب يتعلق بالاستطاعة؛ فلا واجب مع العجزء ولا محرم مع الضرورة
refs.note: Al-Saʿdī Q4: no obligation with inability (formalised as Sadi.operative).

terms.definition: What the Lawgiver commanded not by way of binding, e.g. the regular sunna prayers.
conditions: a command
not binding

terms.definition: What no command or prohibition attaches to in itself, e.g. eating at night in Ramaḍān. Ibn ʿUthaymīn adds that it may take the ruling of what it is a means to. In the ʿādāt the default is ibāḥa and in the ʿibādāt prohibition (al-Saʿdī Q6).
conditions: no amr or nahy attaches to it li-dhātihi

terms.definition: What the Lawgiver prohibited not by way of binding abstention, e.g. taking and giving with the left hand.
conditions: a prohibition
not binding

terms.definition: What the Lawgiver prohibited by way of binding abstention, e.g. disobedience to parents. Al-Saʿdī Q4: there is no prohibition with necessity (ḍarūra).
conditions: a prohibition (nahy)
binding abstention

refs.excerpt_ar: الوجوب يتعلق بالاستطاعة؛ فلا واجب مع العجزء ولا محرم مع الضرورة
refs.note: Al-Saʿdī Q4: no prohibition with necessity.

terms.definition: Ibn ʿUthaymīn: what the effects of performing it follow from, whether an act of worship or a contract; it requires its conditions complete and its impediments absent. Ibn Qudāma defines ṣiḥḥa as the Lawgiver's taking the thing into account with respect to its ruling. Ibn Rajab and al-Saʿdī: a prohibition directed at the act of worship itself or its condition voids it, one directed at something external does not (Ibn Rajab reports two narrations where the prohibition of a condition is not specific to it).
conditions: conditions present
impediments absent

refs.excerpt_ar: فإن فُقِد شرطٌ من الشروط، أو وُجِد مانع من الموانع امتنعت الصحة.
refs.note: Validity fails if a condition is missing or an impediment present.

refs.excerpt_ar: فالصحة: هو اعتبار الشرع الشيء في حق حكمه

refs.note: Prohibition returning to the essence or a specific condition of worship voids it; otherwise two narrations or two wajhs.

terms.definition: Ibn ʿUthaymīn: what the effects of performing it do not follow from, whether worship or contract. Ibn al-Laḥḥām: for the Ḥanbalīs and Shāfiʿīs fāsid and bāṭil are synonyms, whereas Abū Ḥanīfa distinguishes the bāṭil (not legislated at all) from the fāsid (legislated in origin but forbidden for a prohibited attribute); Ibn ʿUthaymīn notes the Ḥanbalīs still distinguish them in ḥajj and marriage. Ibn Rajab: a contract whose sound form entails liability entails it when fāsid too.
conditions: a missing condition or present impediment (Ibn ʿUthaymīn)

refs.note: Buṭlān = fasād for Ḥanbalīs and Shāfiʿīs; Abū Ḥanīfa distinguishes them.

refs.excerpt_ar: فرقوا بينهما بأن الفاسد ما اختلف العلماء في فساده كالنكاح بلا ولي، والباطل ما أجمعوا على بطلانه كنكاح المعتدة.
refs.note: Ibn ʿUthaymīn: the distinction is kept in marriage (disputed vs agreed invalidity).
Liability under a fāsid contract follows its ṣaḥīḥ counterpart.

terms.definition: Al-Kawkab (after al-Qarāfī, also quoted by al-Ṭūfī): what by its existence entails the existence (of the ruling) and by its absence its absence, in itself; 'in itself' excludes cases where a condition is missing or an impediment present (e.g. the niṣāb before the year is complete). Al-Ṭūfī notes that a sharʿī cause, unlike a rational one, need not always produce its effect. Al-Saʿdī Q39 and Ibn Rajab q4: worship and expiations may not precede the cause of obligation but may precede its condition.
conditions: existence entails the ruling, absence its absence, li-dhātihi

refs.excerpt_ar: والسبب في عرف أهل الشرع: "ما يلزم من وجوده الوجود و" يلزم "من عدمه العدم لذاته"
refs.note: Definition of sabab in al-Kawkab with its three restrictions.

refs.excerpt_ar: لا يجوز تقديم العبادات؛ أو الكفارات على سبب الوجوب، ويجوز تقديمها بعد وجود السبب، وقبل شرط الوجوب وتحققه
refs.note: Al-Saʿdī Q39: no performance before the cause, permitted before the condition.
Ibn Rajab: same rule for ʿibādāt.

terms.definition: Ibn Qudāma: what entails, by its absence, the absence of the ruling (iḥṣān for stoning, the year for zakāt); the conditioned does not exist without it, but need not exist when it exists. Al-Kawkab: what by its absence entails absence and by its existence neither existence nor absence, in itself. Conditions are rational, linguistic or sharʿī; al-Kawkab (after al-Qarāfī) says the linguistic 'condition' (if you enter the house you are divorced) is really a sabab.
conditions: absence entails absence of the ruling
existence does not entail the ruling

refs.excerpt_ar: وهو: ما يلزم من انتفائه انتفاء الحكم، كالإحصان مع الرجم، والحول في الزكاة.
الشرط "شرعا" أي في عرف أهل الشرع: "ما يلزم من عدمه العدم" و "لا" يلزم "من وجوده وجود ولا عدم لذاته"
لابد لذلك من أحد أمرين : إما لفقد لازم من لوازمهاء أو لوجود مانع خاص يبطلها
refs.note: Al-Saʿdī Q8: a failed act lacks a required element or has a voiding impediment.

terms.definition: The converse of the sharṭ: what by its existence entails the absence of the ruling (Ibn Qudāma; al-Ṭūfī gives debt with zakāt and fatherhood with retaliation). Al-Kawkab distinguishes an impediment of the cause, which disturbs the cause's ḥikma (debt against the niṣāb), from an impediment of the ruling, which leaves the ḥikma intact.
conditions: its existence entails absence of the ruling

refs.excerpt_ar: وعكس الشرط: المانع: وهو: ما يلزم من وجوده عدم الحكم
ومن أجل كون العلة لا بد من اشتمالها على حكمة تدعو إلى الامتثال، كان مانعها وصفا وجوديا يخل بحكمتها، ويسمى مانع السبب، فإن لم يخل بحكمتها، بل بالحكم فقط، والحكمة باقية، سمي مانع الحكم.
refs.note: Al-Kawkab: māniʿ al-sabab vs māniʿ al-ḥukm.
Ibn Rajab: when a ruling and its impediment coincide, the well-known madhhab is that the ruling does not arise (Ibn Ḥāmid disagrees).

terms.definition: Ibn Qudāma gives two definitions: making the forbidden permitted while the prohibiting factor remains; or what is established against a sharʿī proof because of a preponderant opposing factor. What does not go against a proof is not called rukhṣa even if it is lenient.
conditions: a prohibiting proof still stands
a preponderant opposing factor (e.g. necessity, hardship)

refs.excerpt_ar: والرخصة: استباحة المحظور، مع قيام الحاظر
وقيل: ما ثبت على خلاف دليل شرعي لمعارض راجح
الوجوب يتعلق بالاستطاعة؛ فلا واجب مع العجزء ولا محرم مع الضرورة
refs.note: Al-Saʿdī Q4 (necessity lifts prohibition), the case the Lean readings model; the term rukhṣa itself is not a Lean constant.

terms.definition: Linguistically firm intent. Ibn Qudāma: the ruling established without contravening a sharʿī proof (or: what God made binding on His servants). Ibn al-Laḥḥām, quoting al-Ṭūfī: the ruling established by a sharʿī proof free of an opposing factor, which al-Ṭūfī says covers the obligatory, prohibited and disliked. Not formalised in the Lean modules.

refs.excerpt_ar: فالعزيمة: الحكم الثابت من غير مخالفة دليل شرعي

refs.note: Ibn al-Laḥḥām / al-Ṭūfī's definition and its scope.

terms.definition: Al-Kawkab: technically, that by which correct reflection can lead to a sought-for informative conclusion. Ibn ʿUthaymīn orders the adilla as Book, Sunna, ijmāʿ and qiyās and requires reconciling them before abrogation or preference.

refs.excerpt_ar: الدليل "شرعا" أي في اصطلاح علماء الشريعة: "ما" أي الشيء الذي "يمكن التوصل بصحيح النظر" - متعلق بالتوصل- أي بالنظر الصحيح؛ من باب إضافة الصفة إلى الموصوف "فيه" أي في ذلك الشيء "إلى مطلوب خبري"
وإن تعارضت، وأمكن الجمع وجب الجمع، وإن لم يمكن الجمع عمل بالنسخ إن تمت شروطه.

terms.definition: The agreement of the mujtahids of this umma after the Prophet on a sharʿī ruling. It is also a maslak of the ʿilla (the umma agrees that the ruling's ʿilla is X). Ibn ʿUthaymīn prefers decisive over presumptive ijmāʿ.
conditions: mujtahids
of this umma
after the Prophet
on a sharʿī ruling

refs.excerpt_ar: والمراد بثبوت العلة بالإجماع: أن تجمع الأمة على أن هذا الحكم علته كذا
refs.note: Ijmāʿ as the first maslak of the ʿilla.

terms.definition: Ibn ʿUthaymīn: equating a farʿ with an aṣl in a ruling for an ʿilla uniting them. Ibn Qudāma and al-Ṭūfī: carrying (ḥaml) a farʿ onto an aṣl in a ruling by a common factor; al-Kawkab: returning (radd) a farʿ to an aṣl by a uniting ʿilla. Its pillars are aṣl, farʿ, ʿilla and ḥukm. Ibn Taymiyya (via Ibn al-Qayyim) distinguishes sound qiyās (joining like cases, separating unlike ones), which never contradicts a text, from unsound qiyās.
conditions: four arkān: aṣl, farʿ, ʿilla, ḥukm
not against a stronger proof (Ibn ʿUthaymīn cond. 1)
aṣl ruling by text or ijmāʿ
ʿilla present in the farʿ

refs.excerpt_ar: حمل فرع على أصل في حكم بجامع بينهما
رد فرع إلى أصل بعلة جامعة
ولا بد في كل قياس من أصل، وفرع، وعلة، وحكم
والصحيح هو الذي وردت به الشريعة، وهو الجمع بين المتماثلين والفرق بين المختلفين، فالأول قياس الطرد، والثاني قياس العكس
refs.note: Ibn Taymiyya: sound vs unsound qiyās.

terms.definition: The case compared to. Al-Kawkab: for the jurists it is the locus of the ruling compared to; others say it is the proof of the ruling or the ruling itself, a verbal dispute; al-Ṭūfī likewise reports text (the ribā ḥadīth) or its locus (the six commodities). Conditions: its ruling is established by text or agreement of the disputants (Ibn Qudāma) or by text or ijmāʿ, not by qiyās (Ibn ʿUthaymīn), and is rationally intelligible.
conditions: ruling established by naṣṣ or agreement/ijmāʿ
ruling maʿqūl al-maʿnā
its proof does not already cover the farʿ

refs.excerpt_ar: فالأصل محل الحكم المشبه به
refs.note: What the aṣl is (locus) and the verbal dispute.

refs.excerpt_ar: أحدهما: أن يكون ثابتا بنص، أو اتفاق من الخصمين
refs.note: Ibn Qudāma: established by text or agreement of both disputants.

refs.excerpt_ar: أن يكون حكم الأصل ثابتاً بنص أو إجماع، فإن كان ثابتاً بقياس لم يصح القياس عليه
refs.note: Ibn ʿUthaymīn: by text or ijmāʿ; not by qiyās.

refs.excerpt_ar: أن يكون الحكم معقول المعنى، إذ القياس إنما هو: تعدية الحكم من محل إلى محل بواسطة تعدي المقتضى

terms.definition: The case to which the aṣl's ruling is extended. Its condition is that the ʿilla of the aṣl exist in it as it does in the aṣl (Ibn ʿUthaymīn); al-Ṭūfī accepts presumptive presence. Al-Kawkab: there must be no text on the farʿ's ruling.
conditions: the aṣl's ʿilla present in it
no text already rules it

refs.excerpt_ar: أن تكون العلة موجودة في الفرع كوجودها في الأصل
وشرط الفرع وجود علة الأصل فيه ظنا إذ هو كالقاطع في الشرعيات
وقال الموفق والمجد والطوفي: يشترط لقياس العلة، لا لقياس الدلالة
refs.note: Al-Kawkab: no concordant text on the farʿ.

terms.definition: Ibn Qudāma: the manāṭ (anchor) of the ruling; the sharʿī ʿilla is a sign (ʿalāma), which may be a ruling, a description, simple or compound, positive or negative. Al-Ṭūfī: a sign and identifier which must be transitive (so the restricted ʿilla is disregarded), against al-Shāfiʿī and Abū al-Khaṭṭāb. Ibn ʿUthaymīn requires it to contain a suitable meaning recognised by the sharʿ. Al-Saʿdī Q58 instead says the ʿilla of the ruling is the ḥikma in commanding, forbidding or permitting it.
conditions: present in aṣl and farʿ
suitable meaning (Ibn ʿUthaymīn)
transitive (disputed)

refs.excerpt_ar: ونعني بالعلة: مناط الحكم. وسميت علة؛ لأنها غيرت حال المحل
ومعنى العلة الشرعية: العلامة
refs.note: The sharʿī ʿilla is a sign; kinds of description it may be.

refs.excerpt_ar: أما العلة الشرعية فهي علامة ومعرف، ومن شرطها أن تكون متعدية فلا عبرة بالقاصرة
أن تكون العلة مشتملة على معنى مناسب للحكم يعلم من قواعد الشرع اعتباره
refs.note: Ibn ʿUthaymīn: must contain a suitable meaning.

refs.excerpt_ar: وعلة الحكم هي الحكمة في الأمر به، أو النهي عنه؛ أو إباحته
refs.note: Al-Saʿdī Q58: ʿilla identified with the ḥikma.

terms.definition: The purpose a ruling serves. Al-Kawkab: the ʿilla must contain a ḥikma that calls to compliance, and an impediment of the cause is one that disturbs that ḥikma. Ibn Qudāma and al-Ṭūfī: showing the ḥikma without the ruling (kasr) is not binding, since ḥikmas cannot be measured by opinion. Al-Saʿdī identifies the ʿilla with the ḥikma, where Ibn Qudāma treats the ʿilla as a sign.

refs.excerpt_ar: ومن أجل كون العلة لا بد من اشتمالها على حكمة تدعو إلى الامتثال، كان مانعها وصفا وجوديا يخل بحكمتها، ويسمى مانع السبب، فإن لم يخل بحكمتها، بل بالحكم فقط، والحكمة باقية، سمي مانع الحكم.
refs.note: The ʿilla must contain a ḥikma; māniʿ al-sabab disturbs it.

refs.excerpt_ar: وهو إبداء الحكمة بدون الحكم: فغير لازم
وعلة الحكم هي الحكمة في الأمر به، أو النهي عنه؛ أو إباحته
refs.note: Al-Saʿdī: the ʿilla is the ḥikma.

terms.definition: A description of the case that may serve as the ʿilla. Ibn Qudāma: the sharʿī ʿilla may be an accidental or inherent description, simple or compound, negative or positive, suitable or not. Ibn ʿUthaymīn excludes a ṭardī description (e.g. blackness) as a cause. Sabr enumerates the descriptions in the aṣl and cancels the unfit ones.

refs.excerpt_ar: ومعنى العلة الشرعية: العلامة
refs.note: Kinds of description that can be an ʿilla.

refs.excerpt_ar: أن تكون العلة مشتملة على معنى مناسب للحكم يعلم من قواعد الشرع اعتباره
وهو: حصر الأوصاف" في الأصل المقيس عليه "وإبطال ما لا يصلح
refs.note: Sabr operates on the descriptions of the aṣl.

terms.definition: The proofs that establish the ʿilla, which Ibn Qudāma reduces to text, consensus and extraction (istinbāṭ). Extraction includes munāsaba, sabr wa-taqsīm and dawarān; al-Kawkab lists ijmāʿ, naṣṣ, sabr, munāsaba, shabah, dawarān and discusses ṭard. Preference: an ʿilla by sabr over munāsaba over shabah (al-Kawkab); consensual over textual over extracted (al-Ṭūfī).

refs.excerpt_ar: وأدلة الشرع ترجع إلى "نص" أو "إجماع" أو "استنباط" فهذه ثلاثة أقسام
و" يرجح أحد القياسين ب "سبر، فمناسبة

terms.definition: The ruling exists with the description and ceases with its absence (prohibition with the intoxicating strength of wine). It yields presumption (ẓann) of causality according to most Ḥanbalīs (al-Kawkab, al-Ṭūfī); Ibn Qudāma reports that some require it to be combined with something else. Al-Āmidī and Ibn al-Ḥājib call it ṭard wa-ʿaks.
conditions: ṭard: ruling with the description
ʿaks: no ruling without it

refs.excerpt_ar: النوع الثالث- في إثبات العلة: أن يوجد الحكم بوجودها، ويعدم بعدمها
ويفيد" الدوران "العلة ظنا" عند الأكثر من أصحابنا
refs.note: Al-Kawkab: yields ẓann per most aṣḥāb.

terms.definition: Concomitance of ruling and description without suitability. Proving an ʿilla by its mere constancy (iṭṭirād) is invalid according to Ibn Qudāma and al-Ṭūfī (absence of one defeater is not proof), and al-Kawkab says ṭard alone is not a proof according to the four imams.

refs.excerpt_ar: فأما الدلالة على صحة العلة باطرادها ففاسد
refs.note: Ibn Qudāma: proof by iṭṭirād is void.

refs.excerpt_ar: خاتمة اطراد العلة لا يفيد صحتها
refs.note: Al-Ṭūfī: iṭṭirād does not prove validity.

refs.excerpt_ar: وليس" الطرد "دليلا وحده" عند الأئمة الأربعة وغيرهم
refs.note: Al-Kawkab: not a proof by itself.

terms.definition: Enumerating the descriptions in the aṣl and cancelling those unfit, so that the remainder is the ʿilla (al-Kawkab). Ibn Qudāma: the ruling is caused; the ʿilla is only X or Y; one is void so the other is fixed. The enumeration must be exhaustive, and naqḍ alone does not suffice to cancel a description.
conditions: the ruling is agreed to be caused
exhaustive enumeration (ḥaṣr)
cancellation of all but one

refs.excerpt_ar: وهو: حصر الأوصاف" في الأصل المقيس عليه "وإبطال ما لا يصلح
فنقول: الحكم معلل، ولا علة إلا كذا أو كذا، وقد بطل أحدهما فيتعين الآخر
الأمر الثاني: أن يكون سبره حاصرا لجميع ما يعلل به
ولا يكفيه في إفساد علة خصمه: النقض
refs.note: Naqḍ alone does not cancel a description.

terms.definition: The description coupled with the ruling is suitable: establishing the ruling after it secures a maṣlaḥa (Ibn Qudāma). The munāsib is muʾaththir, mulāʾim or gharīb; some restricted qiyās to the muʾaththir, which Ibn Qudāma rejects. Al-Kawkab also calls it ikhāla and says extracting the ʿilla by it is takhrīj al-manāṭ.

refs.excerpt_ar: ومعناه: أن يكون في إثبات الحكم عقيبه مصلحة
فالمناسب ثلاثة أنواع: مؤثر، وملائم، وغريب
الرابع " من مسالك العلة "المناسبة، و" يقال "الإخالة

terms.definition: Ibn Qudāma: istiṣlāḥ is following the maṣlaḥa mursala; maṣlaḥa is securing benefit or repelling harm. A maṣlaḥa neither attested nor cancelled by the law is called mursala, not qiyās, since qiyās returns to a specific aṣl. Mālik and some Shāfiʿīs accept it as a proof; Ibn Qudāma and, per al-Kawkab, most Ḥanbalīs do not.

refs.excerpt_ar: الرابع من الأصول المختلف فيها: الاستصلاح: وهو: اتباع المصلحة المرسلة. والمصلحة: هي جلب المنفعة، أو دفع المضرة.
فيسمى ذلك مصلحة مرسلة، ولا نسميه قياسا؛ لأن القياس يرجع إلى أصل معين. والصحيح: أن ذلك ليس بحجة
refs.note: Not called qiyās; Ibn Qudāma: not a proof.

refs.excerpt_ar: "وليست هذه المصلحة بحجة" عند الأكثر، خلافا لمالك وبعض الشافعية، وتسمى المصلحة المرسلة.
refs.note: Al-Kawkab: not a proof for most, against Mālik and some Shāfiʿīs.

terms.definition: Al-Qāḍī: the farʿ oscillates between a permitting and a prohibiting aṣl and is joined to the one it resembles more (the slave between the free man and the beast). Sources differ on its authority: two reports from Aḥmad (al-Ṭūfī: the more apparent is that it is valid); al-Kawkab: a proof only where qiyās al-ʿilla is impossible; Ibn ʿUthaymīn calls it weak; Ibn al-Qayyim says God reports it only from the people of falsehood.

refs.excerpt_ar: هو أن يتردد الفرع بين أصلين: حاظر ومبيح، ويكون شبهه بأحدهما أكثر
والثالث: الشبه، وفي صحة التمسك به قولان لأحمد والشافعي - رضي الله عنهما -، والأظهر: نعم لإثارته الظن، خلافا للقاضي
refs.note: Two views from Aḥmad; al-Ṭūfī prefers validity.

refs.excerpt_ar: فإن عدم" إمكان قياس العلة "فحجة" أي فقياس الشبه حجة عندنا
refs.note: Al-Kawkab: only when qiyās al-ʿilla is unavailable.

refs.excerpt_ar: وهذا القسم من القياس ضعيف إذ ليس بينه وبين الأصل علة مناسبة
وأما قياس الشبه فلم يحكه الله سبحانه إلا عن المبطلين
refs.note: Ibn al-Qayyim: reported only from the people of falsehood.

terms.definition: The Lawgiver attaches a ruling to its cause together with descriptions that play no part, which must be set aside so that the ruling extends (the Bedouin who had intercourse in Ramaḍān). Al-Ṭūfī says most deniers of qiyās accept it.

refs.excerpt_ar: وهو: أن يضيف الشارع الحكم إلى سببه، فيقترن به أوصاف لا مدخل لها في الإضافة، فيجب حذفها عن الاعتبار، ليتسع الحكم
وقال به أكثر منكري القياس

terms.definition: The Lawgiver states a ruling without indicating its manāṭ and the mujtahid extracts it by reasoning (intoxication for wine). Ibn Qudāma calls this the disputed qiyās; al-Ṭūfī calls it the qiyās-based ijtihād; al-Kawkab identifies extraction by munāsaba with it.

refs.excerpt_ar: فيستنبط المناط بالرأي والنظر
وهو الاجتهاد القياسي، وأجاز أصحابنا التعبد به عقلا وشرعا، وبه قال عامة الفقهاء والمتكلمين خلافا للظاهرية والنظام
الرابع " من مسالك العلة "المناسبة، و" يقال "الإخالة
refs.note: Al-Kawkab: extraction by munāsaba is takhrīj al-manāṭ.

terms.definition: The general rule (or ʿilla) is agreed or textual, and one verifies it in the particular case (Ibn Qudāma); al-Kawkab: establishing the ʿilla in its individual instances. Al-Shinqīṭī notes that in its first type 'manāṭ' is not the technical ʿilla but the general text being applied.
conditions: the manāṭ is already known by text or agreement

refs.excerpt_ar: ومعناه: أن تكون القاعدة الكلية متفقا عليها، أو منصوصا عليها، ويجتهد في تحقيقها في الفرع
وتحقيقه": أي تحقيق المناط "إثبات العلة في آحاد صورها
refs.note: Al-Kawkab's definitions of the manāṭ operations.

refs.excerpt_ar: والمناطُ هنا ليس بمعناه الاصطلاحي

terms.definition: The objections to a qiyās. Ibn Qudāma lists twelve (istifsār, fasād al-iʿtibār, fasād al-waḍʿ, manʿ, taqsīm, muṭālaba, naqḍ, qawl bi'l-mūjab, qalb, ʿadam al-taʾthīr, muʿāraḍa, tarkīb); al-Kawkab and others count twenty-five. Al-Ṭūfī, al-Kawkab and al-Shinqīṭī say they all reduce to manʿ or muʿāraḍa.

refs.excerpt_ar: قال بعض أهل العلم: يتوجه على القياس اثنا عشر سؤالا
القوادح ترجع إلى المنع في المقدمات، أو المعارضات في الحكم
refs.note: Al-Kawkab: reduce to manʿ or muʿāraḍa; 25.

refs.excerpt_ar: والأسئلة راجعة إلى منع، أو معارضة، وإلا لم يسمع

terms.definition: Denial, by the objector, of the aṣl's ruling, of the ʿilla's existence in the aṣl, of its causality, or of its existence in the farʿ; the soundest view is that the arguer is not cut off by denial of the aṣl ruling (Ibn Qudāma, al-Ṭūfī). Muṭālaba (demanding proof of causality) is the third of these denials.

refs.excerpt_ar: وقد اختلف في انقطاع المستدل عند توجه منع الحكم في الأصل: والصحيح: أنه لا ينقطع
المنع، وهو منع حكم الأصل، ولا ينقطع به المستدل على الأصح
وهي: طلب المستدل بذكر ما يدل على أن ما جعله جامعا هو العلة

terms.definition: Showing the ʿilla without the ruling (Ibn Qudāma, al-Ṭūfī). Whether it voids the ʿilla is disputed; Ibn Qudāma prefers that it is a valid objection and that the arguer should guard his proof against it. Al-Kawkab calls it takhṣīṣ al-ʿilla and records ten views on whether it impairs the ʿilla.

refs.excerpt_ar: ومعناه: إبداء العلة بدون الحكم
وهو إبداء العلة بدون الحكم، وفي بطلان العلة به خلاف
والنقض، ويسمى تخصيص العلة" هو "عدم اطرادها

terms.definition: Whether the ʿilla survives a naqḍ as a proof in the remaining cases, like a specified general term. Sources differ: al-Qāḍī and Abū al-Khaṭṭāb (al-Kawkab) hold naqḍ does not impair it; Ibn Ḥāmid holds it does; Ibn Qudāma distinguishes, voiding the extracted ʿilla but not the textual one when a condition is missing or an impediment present; al-Shinqīṭī prefers the reverse attribution; Ibn al-Qayyim says takhṣīṣ for a missing condition or present impediment is not impossible.

refs.excerpt_ar: والنقض، ويسمى تخصيص العلة" هو "عدم اطرادها
وهذا قول القاضي وأبي الخطاب. وحكاه الآمدي عن أكثر أصحابنا
والقول الثاني: يقدح. اختاره من أصحابنا: ابن حامد وقاله القاضي أيضا
وفرق قوم بين العلة المنصوص عليها، وبين المستنبطة، وجعل نقض المستنبطة مبطلا لها
refs.note: Ibn Qudāma's distinction textual vs extracted.

refs.excerpt_ar: وبالجملة فلا يمتنع تخصيص العلة لفوات شرط أو لقيام مانع

terms.definition: Showing the ḥikma without the ruling. Ibn Qudāma and al-Ṭūfī: not binding, since the ḥikma cannot be measured by opinion; al-Kawkab: the sound view among the aṣḥāb is that kasr does not void the ʿilla, while Ibn Mufliḥ calls it 'naqḍ of the meaning', treated like naqḍ; al-Shinqīṭī holds it impairs wherever naqḍ does.

refs.excerpt_ar: وهو إبداء الحكمة بدون الحكم: فغير لازم
الصحيح عند أصحابنا والأكثر: أن الكسر والنقض المكسور "لا يبطلانها
refs.note: Al-Kawkab: does not void the ʿilla.

refs.excerpt_ar: قال ابن مفلح: الكسر: نقض المعنى. والكلام فيه كالنقض
refs.note: Ibn Mufliḥ: naqḍ of the meaning.

refs.excerpt_ar: فالظاهرُ أنَّ الكسر كالنقض، فعلى أنَّ النقضَ قادحٌ فالكسرُ كذلك

terms.definition: Ibn Qudāma and al-Ṭūfī: the proof mentions something superfluous to establishing the aṣl's ruling, because the ruling holds without it or because it is a ṭardī description. Al-Kawkab frames it as the claim that the description lacks suitability, not raised against qiyās al-dalāla.

refs.excerpt_ar: ومعناه: أن يذكر في الدليل ما يستغنى عنه في إثبات الحكم في الأصل
عدم التأثير، وهو ذكر ما يستغني عنه الدليل في ثبوت حكم الأصل
و "لا يرد" هذا "على قياس الدلالة" قاله الشيخ تقي الدين وابن عقيل

terms.definition: The objector derives from the arguer's own proof, keeping the aṣl and description, a ruling contrary to his (Ibn Qudāma); al-Ṭūfī: attaching the negation of the arguer's ruling to his very ʿilla. Al-Kawkab and Ibn Qudāma count it a kind of muʿāraḍa.

refs.excerpt_ar: ومعناه: أن يذكر لدليل المستدل حكما ينافي حكم المستدل، مع تبقية الأصل والوصف بحالهما
القلب، وهو تعليق نقيض حكم المستدل على علته بعينها
وهو "تعليق نقيض الحكم أو لازمه

terms.definition: Conceding what the arguer made the consequence of his proof while the dispute remains; the last of the objections (Ibn Qudāma, al-Ṭūfī, al-Kawkab).

refs.excerpt_ar: وحقيقته: تسليم ما جعله المستدل موجبا لدليله، مع بقاء الخلاف
القول بالموجب، وهو: تسليم الدليل مع منع المدلول
تسليم مقتضى الدليل مع بقاء النزاع

terms.definition: The objection that the qiyās contradicts a text (Ibn Qudāma, al-Ṭūfī) or a text or ijmāʿ (al-Kawkab), so it is void. Ibn ʿUthaymīn makes non-collision with a stronger proof the first condition of qiyās.

refs.excerpt_ar: وهو أن يقول: هذا قياس يخالف نصا، فيكون باطلا
الثاني: من القوادح "فساد الاعتبار
أن لا يصادم دليلاً أقوى منه

terms.definition: Showing that the ʿilla requires the opposite of the ruling attached to it (Ibn Qudāma, al-Ṭūfī). Al-Kawkab: more specific than fasād al-iʿtibār; the qiyās is not in a form fit to yield the ruling.

refs.excerpt_ar: وهو: أن يبين أن الحكم المعلق على العلة تقتضي العلة نقيضه
وهو اقتضاء العلة نقيض ما علق بها
الثالث: من القوادح "فساد الوضع

terms.definition: Either in the aṣl, showing another cause for its ruling (better, needs no aṣl of its own), or in the farʿ, citing what prevents the ruling there, a stronger proof or a description; Ibn Qudāma and al-Kawkab accept it. With manʿ, it is one of the two kinds to which all objections reduce.

refs.excerpt_ar: وأحسنهما: المعارضة في الأصل؛ لأنه لا يحتاج إلى ذكر غير صلاحية ما يذكره، ولا يحتاج إلى أصل
وهو: أن يذكر في الفرع ما يمتنع معه ثبوت الحكم
المعارضة في الفرع بما يقتضي نقيض حكم المستدل

terms.definition: The objector shows a meaning distinguishing the aṣl from the farʿ so that the farʿ is not joined to it; al-Kawkab says it reduces to muʿāraḍa in the aṣl or farʿ. Ibn al-Qayyim: equating cases that differ in what requires or prevents the ruling is unsound qiyās.

refs.excerpt_ar: وهو إبداء المعترض معنى يحصل به الفرق بين الأصل والفرع حتى لا يلحق به في حكمه
وأما التسوية بينهما في الحكم مع افتراقهما فيما يقتضي الحكم أو يمنعه فهذا هو القياس الفاسد

terms.definition: Ibn Qudāma: istiṣḥāb is holding to a rational or sharʿī proof (original non-liability, a general term until specified, a text until abrogated, a ruling the law shows to continue), resting on a presumptive proof with no changer known. Al-Saʿdī Q11: the presumption is that what was remains, and certainty is not removed by doubt. Ibn Rajab: when two presumptions conflict the stronger is followed; al-Saʿdī Q6: the default in ʿādāt is permission and in ʿibādāt prohibition.

refs.excerpt_ar: فالاستصحاب إذن: عبارة عن التمسك بدليل عقلي أو شرعي، وليس راجعا إلى عدم الدليل، بل إلى دليل ظني مع انتفاء المغير، أو العلم به.
الأصل بقاء ما كان على ما كان، واليقين لا يزول بالشك

terms.definition: The term is used in two senses. Textual: what indicates by itself a preponderant meaning while admitting another (Ibn ʿUthaymīn). Factual (Ibn Rajab): when the aṣl and the ẓāhir conflict, a ẓāhir that is a sharʿī proof (testimony, report) prevails without dispute; one resting on custom, indicators or preponderant belief sometimes prevails, sometimes not, sometimes is disputed.

refs.note: Conflict of aṣl and ẓāhir, four kinds.

terms.definition: Decisive perception (ʿilm: «إدراكاً جازماً», Ibn ʿUthaymīn). Al-Saʿdī Q11: certainty is not removed by doubt. Adopted reading (IQ-21, human review 2026-10-07): a judgement is certain for acting when it is qaṭʿ, or a ẓann whose preponderance is itself known on a dalīl (Ibn Taymiyya: belief in a view's preponderance is ʿilm; al-Rawḍa: God makes ẓann a sign of the obligation, so the obligation is known). A ẓann of unknown preponderance is not yaqīn. Where certainty cannot be reached, one builds on ghalabat al-ẓann (bayt 90).

refs.excerpt_ar: العلم: إدراك الشيء على ما هو عليه إدراكاً جازماً
الأصل بقاء ما كان على ما كان، واليقين لا يزول بالشك
refs.note: Certainty is not removed by doubt.

refs.excerpt_ar: أي استحالة في أن يجعل الله -تعالى- الظن علامة للوجوب، والظن مدرك بالحس، فيكون الوجوب معلوما
refs.note: Ẓann a sign of the obligation, which is then known.

terms.definition: Perceiving a thing with an equal possibility of its opposite (Ibn ʿUthaymīn).

refs.excerpt_ar: شك، وهو إدراك الشيء مع احتمال ضدٍّ مساو.

terms.definition: Perceiving a thing with a weaker possibility of its opposite (Ibn ʿUthaymīn); the weaker side is wahm, equal sides shakk. Ẓann has degrees, the higher called ghalabat al-ẓann (al-Kawkab), and leans on a cause, unlike wahm (al-Rawḍa). Usage: «ʿilm» is said figuratively of presumptive assent («فإن علمتموهن مؤمنات») and «ẓann» of knowledge («الذين يظنون أنهم ملاقو ربهم»), but neither collapses the grades. Whether fiqh, mostly ẓann, is ʿilm is answered several ways: the ruling is known and the ẓann lies on its way (al-Rāzī; al-Ṭūfī finds it contrived and would define fiqh as ẓann); fiqh is maʿrifa covering both (Ibn ʿUthaymīn); Ibn Taymiyya: belief that a view preponderates is ʿilm, the preponderance of one belief over another is ẓann, and fiqh is the former (IQ-21).

refs.excerpt_ar: ظن، وهو إدراك الشيء مع احتمال ضد مرجوح.
ويجب العمل بالظن فيها" أي في علل الأحكام "إجماعا
refs.note: Acting on ẓann in ʿilal obligatory by consensus.

refs.excerpt_ar: ويتفاوت الظن، حتى يقال: غلبة الظن
refs.note: Ẓann has degrees; the higher is ghalabat al-ẓann.

refs.excerpt_ar: فإن الوهم ميل النفس من غير سبب، والظن: ميلها بسبب
refs.note: Wahm inclines without a cause, ẓann with one.

refs.excerpt_ar: يعني أن الظن يطلق ويراد به العلم. ومنه قوله تعالى: {الذين يظنون أنهم ملاقو ربهم}
وأما التصديق الظني: فإطلاقه عليه2 على سبيل المجاز. ومن أمثلته قوله تعالى: {فإن علمتموهن مؤمنات}
refs.note: ʿIlm said figuratively of presumptive assent (60:10).

refs.excerpt_ar: وأجيب عن الأول: بأن الحكم معلوم، والظن في طريقه
refs.note: The standard answer: the ruling is known, the ẓann is on its way.

refs.excerpt_ar: ولو قيل: ظن جملة من الأحكام الشرعية الفرعية، باستنباطها من أدلة تفصيلية، لحصل المقصود وخف الإشكال
refs.note: Al-Ṭūfī's own proposal: define fiqh as ẓann.

terms.definition: An accompanying indication that changes how a text or presumption is taken. The bare command implies obligation unless a qarīna turns it to something else (Ibn al-Laḥḥām, Aḥmad's text). Al-Saʿdī Q52: when qarāʾin are strong they are put before the aṣl. Ibn Rajab: a ẓāhir resting on qarāʾin sometimes prevails over the aṣl and sometimes not; the circumstances (dalālat al-aḥwāl) change the meaning of words.

refs.excerpt_ar: إذا قويت القرائن قدمت على الأصل

refs.note: Ẓāhir based on qarāʾin vs aṣl.

terms.definition: A sign that is not necessarily always accompanied by what it indicates. Ibn ʿUthaymīn defines the waḍʿī rulings as amārāt posited by the Lawgiver; those who admit takhṣīṣ al-ʿilla argue that sharʿī ʿilal are amārāt, which suffice if their ruling is mostly with them (reported by Ibn Qudāma, who answers it). Ibn Rajab allows acting on preponderant belief about time because time has amārāt, unlike completing prayer, ṭahāra or ḥadath.

refs.excerpt_ar: الأحكام الوضعية: ما وضعه الشارع من أمارات، لثبوت أو انتفاء، أو نفوذ، أو إلغاء.
أحدهما: أن علل الشرع أمارات، والأمارة لا توجب وجود حكمها معها أبدا، بل يكفي كونه معها في الأغلب الأكثر.
refs.note: ʿIlal as amārāt (argument reported in Rawḍa).

refs.excerpt_ar: والأول أصح ; لأن الوقت عليه أمارات تعرف بها فاكتفي فيها بالظن الغالب، بخلاف ما لا أمارة عليه من إتمام الصلاة والطهارة والحدث ونحوها

terms.definition: Two proofs facing each other so that one contradicts the other (Ibn ʿUthaymīn). Resolution order: reconcile (jamʿ) if possible, else abrogation if its conditions are met, else preference (tarjīḥ); where none applies, suspension (tawaqquf). Ibn ʿUthaymīn holds such an unresolvable conflict cannot exist in the texts themselves, only in the mujtahid's view.
conditions: jamʿ
then naskh
then tarjīḥ
then tawaqquf

refs.excerpt_ar: وإن تعارضت، وأمكن الجمع وجب الجمع، وإن لم يمكن الجمع عمل بالنسخ إن تمت شروطه.
وإن لم يمكن النسخ وجب الترجيح.

terms.definition: Reconciling two conflicting proofs so each is acted on; it comes first, and abrogation requires that reconciliation be impossible (Ibn ʿUthaymīn).

refs.excerpt_ar: وإن تعارضت، وأمكن الجمع وجب الجمع، وإن لم يمكن الجمع عمل بالنسخ إن تمت شروطه.
تعذر الجمع بين الدليلين، فإن أمكن الجمع فلا نسخ لإمكان العمل بكل منهما.
refs.note: Naskh conditional on impossibility of jamʿ.

terms.definition: Lifting the ruling of a sharʿī proof, or its wording, by a proof from the Book and Sunna. Conditions include that reconciliation be impossible and the later date of the abrogating text be known.
conditions: jamʿ impossible
the abrogating proof known to be later

refs.excerpt_ar: تعذر الجمع بين الدليلين، فإن أمكن الجمع فلا نسخ لإمكان العمل بكل منهما.

terms.definition: When neither reconciliation nor abrogation is possible, preference is obligatory (Ibn ʿUthaymīn: text over ẓāhir, ẓāhir over muʾawwal, manṭūq over mafhūm, the jalī qiyās over the khafī). Among ʿilal, Ibn Qudāma says an ʿilla is preferred by what a report is preferred by; al-Kawkab ranks sabr over munāsaba over shabah.

refs.excerpt_ar: وإن لم يمكن النسخ وجب الترجيح.
قال أصحابنا: ترجح العلة بما يرج به الخبر
refs.note: Ibn Qudāma: ʿilla preferred as reports are.

refs.excerpt_ar: و" يرجح أحد القياسين ب "سبر، فمناسبة
ويقدم من القياس: الجلي على الخفي

terms.definition: Ibn ʿUthaymīn: where two general texts conflict and nothing specifies one by the other, each is acted on where they do not conflict and judgement is suspended where they do. Ibn Rajab reports that Aḥmad suspended judgement on the two-men 'raven' divorce case. Ibn Taymiyya extends it to the single jurist: «وحيث لا يعلم الرجحان فهو متوقف لا قول له». Adopted in the kernel (IQ-21, human review): a ẓann of unknown preponderance is suspended in Qawaid.update, inert as a challenger and counted as shakk as the incumbent.

refs.excerpt_ar: وجب العمل بكل منهما فيما لا يتعارضان فيه، والتوقف في الصورة التي يتعارضان فيها.
ولنا وجه آخر بوجوب اعتزال كل منهما زوجته حتى يتيقن الأمر ونص عليه أحمد رحمه الله في رواية عبد الله ونقل حرب عن أحمد رحمه الله أنه ذكر هذه المسألة فتوقف فيها
refs.note: Ibn Rajab q14: Aḥmad's tawaqquf (and the iʿtizāl wajh).

refs.excerpt_ar: وحيث لا يعلم الرجحان فهو متوقف لا قول له
refs.note: Ibn Taymiyya: no known preponderance, no view.

terms.definition: A term encompassing all its individuals without limit. Al-Saʿdī Q59–60: an indefinite after negation, prohibition or condition, the particles man, mā, ayy, matā, generic al- and the annexed singular are general. Ibn al-Laḥḥām: the singular with al- is general unless there is a qarīna of ʿahd. The generality of the wording, not the specific occasion, counts (Ibn ʿUthaymīn; Ibn al-Laḥḥām q61, with a second view reported).

refs.note: Singular with al- general absent ʿahd.
ʿUmūm al-lafẓ vs khuṣūṣ al-sabab (two views).

terms.definition: A term indicating something limited to a person or number, such as proper names, demonstratives and numbers.

Taking some individuals out of the general term. Its proof is connected (e.g. istithnāʾ: removing some individuals by illā or its sisters) or separate. Ibn Rajab: custom and usage specify the general (ʿurf).

refs.note: Record mislabelled 'fa-min al-mukhaṣṣiṣ al-muttaṣil': it is the definition of al-istithnāʾ, a connected specifier.

terms.definition: A qarīna that al- refers to a known referent; then the singular with al- is not general but turns to the referent (Ibn al-Laḥḥām q52).

refs.note: Generality unless a qarīna of ʿahd.

terms.definition: Ibn ʿUthaymīn: what indicates the reality without restriction ('freeing a slave'). Ibn al-Laḥḥām: what applies to one unspecified individual by a reality common to its genus. When muṭlaq and muqayyad differ in ruling one is not carried on the other (no dispute reported).

refs.note: Ibn al-Laḥḥām's definition and the carrying rule.

terms.definition: Ibn ʿUthaymīn: what indicates the reality with a restriction ('a believing slave'). Ibn al-Laḥḥām: what applies to a specified individual or one described by something added to its genus. Al-Saʿdī Q29: an utterance must be restricted by its attachments (description, condition, exception).

refs.excerpt_ar: يجب تقييد اللفظ بملحقاته من وصف؛»؛ أو شرط,؛ أو استثناء؛ أو غيرها

terms.definition: Dalīl al-khiṭāb: inferring from the singling out of something by mention that the ruling is negated for what lies outside it (the 'grazing' sheep). A proof for Aḥmad, al-Shāfiʿī, Mālik and most theologians; Abū Ḥanīfa and some theologians deny it. Al-Kawkab: it is not taken when the qualifier follows the usual case (khuruj makhraj al-ghālib).
conditions: not where the unmentioned is more or equally entitled (then mafhūm al-muwāfaqa)
not where the qualifier follows the usual case

refs.excerpt_ar: الضرب الرابع: دليل الخطاب: ومعناه: الاستدلال بتخصيص الشيء بالذكر على نفي الحكم عما عداه. ويسمى مفهوم المخالفة
وهذا حجة في قول إمامنا، والشافعي، ومالك، وأكثر المتكلمين. وقالت طائفة منهم، وأبو حنيفة: لا دلالة له
refs.note: Ḥujja for the three imams; denied by Abū Ḥanīfa.

refs.excerpt_ar: "ولا خرج مخرج الغالب" فأما إن خرج مخرج الغالب فلا يعتبر مفهومه

terms.definition: Speech containing a demand for action by way of superiority (Ibn ʿUthaymīn). Unqualified, it implies obligation unless a qarīna turns it elsewhere (Ibn al-Laḥḥām: Aḥmad's text). Commanding a thing is prohibiting its opposites in meaning, not wording (Ibn al-Laḥḥām q48).

refs.excerpt_ar: الأمر: قول يتضمن طلب الفعل على وجه الاستعلاء

terms.definition: Speech containing a demand to refrain by way of superiority, in the form lā tafʿal (Ibn ʿUthaymīn). Unqualified it requires prohibition (Ibn al-Laḥḥām) and, per Ibn ʿUthaymīn, also the invalidity of what is prohibited; whether a prohibition voids worship depends on whether it returns to the act, its condition or something external (Ibn Rajab q9, al-Saʿdī Q38).

refs.excerpt_ar: النهي: قول يتضمن طلب الكف على وجه الاستعلاء بصيغة مخصوصة هي المضارع المقرون بلا الناهية
صيغة النهي عند الإطلاق تقتضي تحريم المنهي عنه وفساده.

terms.definition: Ibn Rajab: the causes of liability are three: contract, hand (possession) and destruction (itlāf). A contract whose valid form entails liability entails it when invalid too. Al-Saʿdī Q14: loss in a trustee's hand is not compensable without transgression or negligence, in a wrongdoer's hand it is; Q18: fungibles are compensated in kind, others by value.
conditions: a cause: ʿaqd, yad or itlāf

refs.excerpt_ar: التلف في يد الأمين غير مضمون إذا لم يتعد؛ أو يفرط؛

terms.definition: Al-Saʿdī: the trustee (amīn) holds another's property with the owner's or the law's consent; loss with him is not compensable unless he transgresses or is negligent. Ibn Rajab: the very meaning of amāna is absence of liability, so a trustee's word on loss is accepted; a pure trust (maḥḍa), held only for the owner's benefit like a deposit, is voided by transgression, while a trust that includes another matter (mutaḍammina) is not, on the sound view. Al-Saʿdī Q43: one who took the thing for his own benefit is not believed on its return; for the owner's benefit he is. Lean encodes Q43's distinction, not Ibn Rajab's voiding rule.
conditions: held with the owner's or the law's permission
no transgression or negligence

refs.excerpt_ar: الأمين: هو الذي في يده مال غيره برضى المالك، أو برضى

refs.note: Amāna means no liability; trustee believed on loss.
Maḥḍa voided by taʿaddī; mutaḍammina not.

refs.excerpt_ar: ما أخذه لمصلحة مالكه خاصة كالمودع فهو أمين محض لكن إذا تلفت الوديعة من بين ماله ففي ضمانه خلاف
refs.note: Ibn Rajab: what he took solely for the owner's benefit (the depositee) is a trustee outright (amīn maḥḍ), «لكن» if the deposit perishes from among his own property his liability is disputed.

refs.excerpt_ar: من قبض العين لحظ نفسه لم يقبل قوله في الرد، فإن قبضه لحظ مالكه قبل

terms.definition: Directly destroying by an act that requires it, or wrongfully setting up a cause that leads to destruction (Ibn Rajab). Al-Saʿdī Q13: the deliberate, the ignorant and the forgetful are equal in it. Destroying a thing to repel its harm is not compensable; destroying it to benefit from it is (Ibn Rajab q26, al-Saʿdī Q36).

refs.note: Itlāf as a cause of ḍamān.

refs.excerpt_ar: الإتلاف يستوي فيه المتعمد»؛ والجاهل؛ والناسي

refs.note: Destroying to repel harm vs to benefit.

refs.excerpt_ar: من أتلف شيئا لينتفع به ضمنه؛ ومن أتلفه دفعاً لمضرته فلا ضمان عليه

terms.definition: Al-Saʿdī Q25: lots are prescribed when the entitled is unknown and division impossible. Ibn Rajab q160 uses lots to distinguish the entitled when an entitlement belongs to an unspecified one among equals, and also to distinguish a specific entitled person from those he is confused with, in property and (per the madhhab) marriages, but not for lineage. The sources differ on whether divisibility excludes lots in the second case.

refs.excerpt_ar: تشرع القرعة إذا جهل المستحق, وتعذرت القسمة

refs.note: Ibn Rajab's two uses of qurʿa.

terms.definition: When two acts of worship of one kind meet, their acts merge and one performance suffices. Ibn Rajab requires that they fall at one time and that neither be qaḍāʾ or follow the other; al-Saʿdī Q41 requires that their purpose be one.
conditions: same genus
Ibn Rajab: same time, neither qaḍāʾ nor tabaʿ
al-Saʿdī: same purpose

refs.excerpt_ar: إذا اجتمعت عبادتان من جنس واحد تداخلت أفعالهماء واكتفي عنهما بفعل واحد إذا كان مقصودهما واحدا

terms.definition: What is not established independently may be established as a dependent: e.g. women's testimony to birth establishes lineage, though their testimony to lineage alone does not (Ibn Rajab q133; al-Saʿdī Q50).

refs.excerpt_ar: يثبت تبعاً ما لا يثبت استقلالاً

terms.definition: Al-Saʿdī Q9: custom is referred to in every ruling the Lawgiver laid down without defining its measure (receipt, safekeeping, negligence). Ibn Rajab: custom specifies general terms, without dispute where usage has made a customary reality, and usage specifies on the text. Ibn ʿUthaymīn: the customary reality is a term used for what it was set for in custom.

refs.excerpt_ar: العرف والعادة يرجع إليه في كل حكم حكم به الشارع؛ ولم يحده بحد
والحقيقة العرفية هي: اللفظ المستعمل فيما وضع له في العرف.

terms.definition: Abstaining from one's wife when a divorce may have taken effect. Ibn Rajab reports Aḥmad's text that two men whose oaths make one wife divorced abstain until certain, and Ibn Taymiyya's reading of Aḥmad: whenever divorce is tied to a condition that may have occurred, the husband abstains until he knows it has not. Al-Saʿdī instead says that on doubt whether the condition occurred one builds on its non-occurrence (the marriage stands), precaution being commendable. Not formalised in the Lean modules.

refs.excerpt_ar: قال الشيخ تقي الدين تأملت نصوص أحمد فوجدته يأمر باعتزال الرجل امرأته في كل يمين حلف الرجل عليها بالطلاق وهو لا يدري أهو بار فيها أم لا؟ حتى يستيقن أنه بار
refs.note: Ibn Taymiyya on Aḥmad's texts (in Ibn Rajab q160).

refs.excerpt_ar: وحاصله أنه متى علق الطلاق بشرط وأمكن وجوده فإنه يعتزل امرأته حتى يعلم انتفاؤه.
refs.note: Summary: abstain until the condition is known not to have occurred.

refs.excerpt_ar: ولنا وجه آخر بوجوب اعتزال كل منهما زوجته حتى يتيقن الأمر ونص عليه أحمد رحمه الله في رواية عبد الله ونقل حرب عن أحمد رحمه الله أنه ذكر هذه المسألة فتوقف فيها
refs.note: Ibn Rajab q14: the iʿtizāl wajh and Aḥmad's tawaqquf.

refs.excerpt_ar: وعلى عدم وجود الشرط الذي علق عليه إذا شك في وجوده
refs.note: Al-Saʿdī: on doubt, build on the condition not having occurred.

refs.excerpt_ar: ولو سلك العبد طريق الاحتياط كان حسناً.
refs.note: Al-Saʿdī: taking the path of precaution is good.

terms.definition: Ibn Rajab q106: the unknown is treated as non-existent, even if the presumption is its continuance, when knowledge of it is despaired of or its consideration is burdensome. Al-Saʿdī Q20: when the right-holder cannot be identified he is treated as non-existent and the property goes to the most beneficial use.
conditions: knowledge despaired of or too burdensome

refs.excerpt_ar: إذا تعذر معرفة من له الحق جُعل كالمعدوم

terms.definition: Perceiving a thing as it is, decisively (Ibn ʿUthaymīn); opposed to simple and compound ignorance and distinguished from ẓann, wahm and shakk. Al-Kawkab lists four uses: literal (what admits no contrary), bare perception, assent decisive or (figuratively) presumptive, and acquaintance. Ibn Taymiyya: what God commands is followed by ʿilm, since the jurist knows which proof preponderates; most fiqh people need is established by text or consensus.

refs.excerpt_ar: فرق بين اعتقاد الرجحان ورجحان الاعتقاد أما اعتقاد الرجحان فهو علم والمجتهد ما عمل إلا بذلك العلم وهو اعتقاد رجحان هذا على هذا وأما رجحان هذا الاعتقاد على هذا الاعتقاد فهو الظن؛ لكن لم يكن ممن قال الله فيه: {إن يتبعون إلا الظن} بل هنا ظن رجحان هذا وظن رجحان ذاك وهذا الظن هو الراجح ورجحانه معلوم
refs.note: Ibn Taymiyya: belief in preponderance is ʿilm; preponderance of a belief is ẓann; «لكن» this ẓann is not the blamed ẓann of {إن يتبعون إلا الظن}: «هذا الظن هو الراجح ورجحانه معلوم».

refs.excerpt_ar: فالفقه هو علمه برجحان هذا الدليل وهذا الظن
refs.note: Fiqh is the jurist's knowledge that this proof and this ẓann preponderate.

refs.excerpt_ar: وحيث لا يعلم الرجحان فهو متوقف لا قول له
refs.note: Where preponderance is not known: suspension, no view.

refs.excerpt_ar: جمهور مسائل الفقه التي يحتاج إليها الناس ويفتون بها هي ثابتة بالنص أو الإجماع
refs.note: Most fiqh people need is established by text or consensus.

terms.gloss: preponderant belief (also al-ẓann al-ghālib, ghālib al-ẓann; the verb: ghalaba ʿalā ẓannih)
terms.definition: The higher degree of ẓann. Ibn ʿUthaymīn, bayt 90: «وإن تعذر اليقين فارجعا لغالب الظن تكن متبعا», i.e. «إذا تعذر اليقين رجعنا إلى غلبة الظن»; with no preponderant belief one returns to the aṣl. It suffices to perform worship or a contract (Ibn Rajab 68) and is put before the aṣl where strong indications support it (al-Saʿdī Q52), but not against an aṣl that certainty can still reach, nor where Aḥmad's naṣṣ requires certainty (dawn in Ramaḍān, Ibn Rajab 159). Al-Saʿdī: management (taṣarruf) rests on it, rulings have fixed routes.
conditions: certainty is unattainable
the belief rests on a cause (amāra), not mere inclination
no aṣl that certainty can reach is displaced by it
its error has not become evident

refs.note: His commentary: the rule, its proofs (64:16, 2:185, Ibn Masʿūd's ḥadīth «فليتحر الصواب»), and its limits.

refs.excerpt_ar: وإن لم يكن غلبة ظن رجعنا إلى الأصل، وهو البناء على اليقين
refs.note: With no preponderant belief, back to the aṣl.

refs.excerpt_ar: عمدة التصرف على غلبة الظن، بخلاف الأحكام، فإن طرقها مضبوطة
refs.note: Al-Saʿdī: management rests on preponderant belief; rulings have fixed routes.

refs.excerpt_ar: منها: تقديم غلبة الظن في المواضع التي يقدم فيها على  الأصل
refs.note: Al-Saʿdī Q52: preponderant belief put before the aṣl in its places.

terms.gloss: a belief whose error has become evident
terms.definition: «لا عبرة بالظن البين خطؤه»: no regard is paid to a belief once its error is evident (al-Mardāwī, al-Taḥbīr; al-Kawkab: «ولا يلتفت إلى ظنه الذي بان خطؤه»). Ibn ʿUthaymīn: one who ended the prayer on a preponderant belief of four, then learned it was three, cannot plead that worship suffices with preponderant belief, «لأنه تبين الخطأ». The limit is «الاجتهاد لا ينقض بالاجتهاد»: the error must be shown by what is decisive (a mufti is liable when «بان خطؤه بدليل قاطع»), not by a second ijtihād. Some domains keep the act even after a certain error: qibla, «سواء كان خطؤه يقينا أو عن اجتهاد», and zakāt given to one believed poor.
conditions: the error is shown by what is decisive (qaṭʿ), not by another ijtihād
the domain is not one where the act stands regardless (qibla, zakāt)

refs.excerpt_ar: لبقاء الوقت، ولا عبرة بالظن البين خطؤه
ولا يلتفت إلى ظنه الذي بان خطؤه
refs.note: Al-Kawkab: the same, of a belief that time would run out.

refs.excerpt_ar: الجواب: لا، لأنه تبين الخطاء، فيجب عليه أن يكمل أربعا
refs.note: Ibn ʿUthaymīn: an evident error undoes reliance on preponderant belief.

refs.excerpt_ar: فإن عمل بفتياه في إتلاف فبان خطؤه بدليل قاطع ضمنه
refs.note: Error shown by a decisive proof.

refs.excerpt_ar: كمن صلى صلاتين باجتهادين إلى جهتين في وقتين، ولم يتبين أنه أخطأ؛ ولأن الاجتهاد لا ينقض بالاجتهاد
refs.note: Ijtihād is not undone by ijtihād.

refs.excerpt_ar: هذا المذهب، وعليه الأصحاب، سواء كان خطؤه يقينا أو عن اجتهاد
refs.note: Qibla: no repetition even after a certain error.

terms.gloss: misappropriation from the booty before its division
terms.definition: Taking from the war booty before it is divided. On a riwāya the ghāll forfeits his own share; Ibn Rajab applies it to theft from the booty when that is treated as ghulūl, so the thief bears the restitution and loses his share, «وقد يكون قدر السرقة وأقل وأكثر». As used in the cited text; the corpus holds no formal definition.
conditions: the taking is from the booty before division
forfeiture of the share is a riwāya, not agreed

terms.definition: A lost item picked up by a finder. After the year of announcement it is owned «لجهالة ربها», and what is not ownable is given in charity on the owner's behalf (al-ṣaḥīḥ): an instance of treating the unknown owner as non-existent (qāʿida 106). Whether ownership comes automatically or by the finder's choice is two wujūh (Ibn Rajab elsewhere), not modelled.
conditions: the year of announcement has passed
the owner remains unknown

terms.gloss: confession, acknowledgement of a right against oneself
terms.definition: Acknowledging a right that lies against oneself. Al-Saʿdī Q55: there is no excuse for one who confesses, even if he then claims error. Ibn al-Laḥḥām uses it as the model for a right against oneself being heard after denial: «كما لو أقر بالحق بعد جحوده».
conditions: the right lies against the speaker
in the rights of persons (Q55's scope)

refs.excerpt_ar: والفرق بين النصين أن الشهادة حق عليه فتسمع بعد النفي كما لو أقر بالحق بعد جحوده والبينة حق له فلا تسمع كما لو ادعى الخق بعد أن نفاه
refs.note: Ibn al-Laḥḥām: confession after denial, the model for a right against oneself.

terms.gloss: proof brought by a claimant (typically witnesses)
terms.definition: The proof a claimant brings for his claim. Ibn al-Laḥḥām treats it as a right for the claimant: one who said «لا بينة لي» and then brings one is not heard (al-manṣūṣ; Ibn ʿAqīl: heard), «كما لو ادعى الحق بعد أن نفاه». As used in the cited text.
conditions: a right for the one who brings it

refs.excerpt_ar: والفرق بين النصين أن الشهادة حق عليه فتسمع بعد النفي كما لو أقر بالحق بعد جحوده والبينة حق له فلا تسمع كما لو ادعى الخق بعد أن نفاه
refs.note: The farq: bayyina is a right for him.

terms.gloss: al-manī: the fluid of janāba (not «semen» at large, which also covers al-madhy and al-wadī)
terms.definition: Of what exits from the front passage, the one that obliges ghusl and is ṭāhir, as al-Saʿdī reports the division (F120: «ومنه طاهر يوجب الغسل وهو المني»). Its ghusl rests on al-Māʾida 6 and al-Nisāʾ 43, on ʿAlī's «فإذا فضخت الماء فاغتسل» (Abū Dāwūd 206) and Umm Salama's «نعم إذا رأت الماء» (al-Bukhārī 282); its ṭahāra on ʿĀʾisha's «كنت أفرك المني من ثوب رسول الله ﷺ فيصلي فيه» (Abū Dāwūd 372). al-Albānī grades all three ṣaḥīḥ (al-Irwāʾ 125, 126, 180).
conditions: ṭāhir: not washed as a najāsa
obliges ghusl (rafʿ al-ḥadath al-akbar), not wuḍūʾ only

refs.excerpt_ar: كنت أفرك المنى من ثوب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم يذهب فيصلى به
refs.note: al-Irwāʾ 180, «* صحيح»: al-manī is rubbed off and prayed in.

refs.excerpt_ar: إذا رأيت المذى فاغسل ذكرك وتوضأ وضوءك للصلاة , فإذا فضخت الماء فاغتسل
refs.note: al-Irwāʾ 125, «* صحيح»: al-madhy obliges washing and wuḍūʾ, al-manī ghusl.

terms.gloss: al-madhy: the fluid that obliges washing and wuḍūʾ, not ghusl
terms.definition: Of what exits from the front passage, the one that is najis and obliges washing the private part and wuḍūʾ, not ghusl (F120: «ومنه نجس ينقض الوضوء ويوجب غسله، وغسل الذكر والأنثيين منه وهو المذي»). It rests on ʿAlī's ḥadīth «يغسل ذكره ويتوضأ» (Muslim 303) and «إذا رأيت المذي فاغسل ذكرك، وتوضأ وضوءك للصلاة» (Abū Dāwūd 206), ṣaḥīḥ in al-Albānī's verdict (al-Irwāʾ 108, 125).
conditions: najis
obliges wuḍūʾ, not ghusl

refs.excerpt_ar: قوله فى المذى: " يغسل ذكره ويتوضأ ". متفق عليه
refs.note: al-Irwāʾ 108, «* صحيح»: al-madhy obliges washing and wuḍūʾ.

terms.gloss: al-wadī: ruled as al-madhy, on an athar
terms.definition: Ruled as al-madhy: washing and wuḍūʾ, not ghusl. Its support is the athar of Ibn ʿAbbās only («وأما المذي والودي فقال: اغسل ذكرك أو مذاكيرك وتوضأ وضوءك للصلاة»), which al-Albānī marks «هذا موقوف» and whose standing as ḥujja alone he calls disputed (Tamām al-Minna). The register records it as an athar, below a marfūʿ naṣṣ.
conditions: support: athar mawqūf (Ibn ʿAbbās), not a marfūʿ naṣṣ

refs.excerpt_ar: أما المني فهو الذي منه الغسل وأما المذي والودي فقال: اغسل ذكرك أو مذاكيرك وتوضأ وضوءك للصلاة
refs.note: Tamām al-Minna: the athar of Ibn ʿAbbās (al-Bayhaqī), as quoted.

refs.excerpt_ar: هذا موقوف والاستدلال به وحده - مع أنه مختلف في صلاحيته للاحتجاج به
refs.note: al-Albānī on it: mawqūf, disputed as a sole ḥujja.

terms.gloss: al-najāsa: a physical impurity, removed (izāla); not ḥadath
terms.definition: A physical impurity, which is removed (izāla), not lifted; removing it is valid without intention (F68), and tayammum is not made for it (F121: «النجاسات كلها لا تيمم عنها، وإنما يتيمم عن الأحداث»). Ibn al-Qayyim: «ما فرق الله بينه من إزالة النجاسة ورفع الحدث». The English «impurity» does not distinguish it from ḥadath; the register names it.

refs.excerpt_ar: وجمعتم بين ما فرق الله بينه من إزالة النجاسة ورفع الحدث
refs.note: Iʿlām: najāsa is removed and ḥadath lifted, two things God separated.

terms.gloss: al-ḥadath: the state lifted (rafʿ) by wuḍūʾ or ghusl; not najāsa
terms.definition: The state that bars prayer and is lifted (rafʿ) by wuḍūʾ (minor) or ghusl (major, janāba), with intention (F68); tayammum is made for it alone (F121). Ibn al-Qayyim: «ما فرق الله بينه من إزالة النجاسة ورفع الحدث».

refs.excerpt_ar: وجمعتم بين ما فرق الله بينه من إزالة النجاسة ورفع الحدث
refs.note: Iʿlām: najāsa is removed and ḥadath lifted.

terms.gloss: al-ṭahūr: water ṭāhir in itself that also purifies (lifts ḥadath, removes najāsa)
terms.definition: Water that is ṭāhir and purifies: «وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً طَهُورًا» (al-Furqān 48); of the sea, «هو الطهور ماؤه الحل ميتته» (Abū Dāwūd 83; al-Irwāʾ 9, ṣaḥīḥ). al-Saʿdī holds that water stays ṭahūr until najāsa changes it (F19: «وأن الماء باق على طهوريته حتى تغيره النجاسة»).

refs.excerpt_ar: وأن الماء باق على طهوريته حتى تغيره النجاسة
refs.note: al-Saʿdī: water stays ṭahūr until najāsa changes it.

refs.excerpt_ar: قوله فى البحر: " هو الطهور ماؤه , الحل ميتته "

terms.gloss: al-ṭāhir: not najis; of water in the madhhab, also a middle class (ṭāhir, not purifying)
terms.definition: What is not najis (al-manī is ṭāhir: F120 «ومنه طاهر يوجب الغسل وهو المني»). In the madhhab's division of water it is also a middle class between ṭahūr and najis: water a ṭāhir substance has changed loses its ṭahūriyya («وأنه يسلبه الطهورية في الأول دون الثاني»). al-Saʿdī grades that farq weak and holds the water ṭahūr (F19). So «pure water» must say which: ṭahūr (purifying) or ṭāhir (not najis, and in the madhhab not purifying).

refs.excerpt_ar: وأنه يسلبه الطهورية في الأول دون الثاني
refs.note: The madhhab's middle class: water a ṭāhir substance changed on purpose loses its ṭahūriyya.

refs.excerpt_ar: ومنه طاهر يوجب الغسل وهو المني

terms.gloss: al-ṭahāra: being ṭāhir; of a person, free of ḥadath (lifted) and of najāsa (removed)
terms.definition: The state of being ṭāhir. Of a person it has two parts the law keeps apart: freedom from ḥadath, lifted by wuḍūʾ or ghusl with intention, and freedom from najāsa, removed without it (F68; Ibn al-Qayyim: «ما فرق الله بينه من إزالة النجاسة ورفع الحدث»). Of a thing: freedom from najāsa.

refs.excerpt_ar: وجمعتم بين ما فرق الله بينه من إزالة النجاسة ورفع الحدث
refs.note: Iʿlām: removing najāsa and lifting ḥadath are two things.

terms.gloss: al-maḥḍ: sheer, unmixed (a «pure means», a «purely God's» right); not a purity term
terms.definition: Sheer, unmixed: a «pure means» (wasīla maḥḍa, Q40) or a right that is God's alone («الحق فيها لله متمحض», F13). The English «pure» in this sense says nothing of ṭahāra.

refs.excerpt_ar: إلا أن يكون المقدور عليه وسيلة محضة
refs.note: Q40: a part that is a pure means (wasīla maḥḍa) is not due by itself.

refs.excerpt_ar: وهذه الحق فيها لله متمحض
refs.note: F13: here the right is purely God's.

terms.gloss: al-ghusl: the full ritual bath that lifts the major ḥadath (janāba, ḥayḍ); not ghasl
terms.definition: Washing the whole body with intention to lift the major ḥadath: «وَإِن كُنتُمْ جُنُبًا فَاطَّهَّرُوا» (al-Māʾida 6), «حَتَّىٰ تَغْتَسِلُوا» (al-Nisāʾ 43), «فإذا فضخت الماء فاغتسل» (Abū Dāwūd 206). al-Saʿdī: «طهارة الحدث الأكبر» against «طهارة الحدث الأصغر» (F52). Unvowelled, الغسل is also al-ghasl; the register vowels it and names which.

refs.excerpt_ar: التفريق في طهارة الحدث الأكبر، وطهارة الحدث الأصغر
refs.note: F52: the ṭahāra of the major ḥadath (ghusl) and of the minor (wuḍūʾ).

terms.gloss: al-ghasl: washing a limb or a thing (in wuḍūʾ, or of najāsa); not ghusl
terms.definition: Washing a limb or a thing: the limbs in wuḍūʾ («فَاغْسِلُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ», al-Māʾida 6), or a najāsa away («سبع غسلات إحداها بتراب», F70; «يغسل ذكره ويتوضأ», Muslim 303). Unvowelled, الغسل is also al-ghusl; the register vowels it and names which.

refs.excerpt_ar: التي لا بد فيها من سبع غسلات إحداها بتراب ونحوه
refs.note: F70: seven washings (ghasalāt) for the heavy najāsa.
